newsitem.title: UK: Taleban takeover of Afghanistan "positive" - Unocal.
newsitem.headline: Taleban takeover of Afghanistan "positive" - Unocal.

text.p: U.S. energy company Unocal Corp., seeking to build both a gas and an oil pipeline across Afghanistan from Turkmenistan to Pakistan, said Tuesday it saw the Taleban Islamic movement's dominance in Afghanistan as a possibly "positive development."
Chris Taggart, Executive Vice President of Unocal International Energy Ventures Ltd., told Reuters, "We regard it (the current situation in Afghanistan) as very positive.
"What is needed is a single government which has control of the country and the broad support of the people, leading to international recognition.
"I understand Pakistan has already recognised the (Taleban) government. If the U.S.A. follows, it will lead the way to international lending agencies coming in.
"If the Taleban leads to stability and international recognition, then it's positive."

Unocal and Saudi Arabia's Delta Oil Co. are looking to build a gas pipeline from Turkmenistan's Dauletabad field across Afghanistan to Pakistan, a distance of 870 to 890 miles, at a cost of $2 billion.

The two also want to build an oil pipeline from Chardzhou in central Turkmenistan to Pakistan's Arabian Sea coast, running 1000 miles, also transiting Afghanistan. This line is expected to cost $2.5 billion.
"The projects are now more likely to succeed than they were two weeks ago," said Taggart.
